{
  "thinking": "The table's empty and the clock's running. A fish has a clean outline that a judge can read from fallen dominoes alone, so I'll grab the pad and push for it.",
  "say": "Let's do a fish! Clean outline, and the tail fin and top fin make it easy to recognize. I've got the pad, so I'll sketch it now and we can trace it.",
  "to": "everyone",
  "eagerness": 8,
  "pad": "take",
  "do": "continue"
}

{
  "thinking": "The round just started and the table is empty. Nobody has the pad yet, so I'll pick it up and suggest a fish, whose outline and tail should read clearly to a judge.",
  "say": "Shall I grab the pad? I'm thinking a fish. A big body with a forked tail should read clearly from the outline alone.",
  "to": "everyone",
  "eagerness": 6,
  "pad": "take",
  "do": "continue",
  "notes": "Round 1 starting, table empty. I hold the pad and proposed a fish with a forked tail. Next: sketch the fish outline with stroke 1 starting at the left end (the start), then trace it once the others agree."
}

{
  "thinking": "Nobody has picked a subject or the pad yet, and the 10 minutes are ticking. I'll take the pad and sketch a simple fish. Its tail fin and pinch point make a clear outline, and I'll set the start at the tail so everything flows toward the head.",
  "say": "Okay, I'm grabbing the pad. How about a fish? Clear outline, and the tail fin makes it easy to recognise. I'll sketch it now, and the tail pinch is where we start the run.",
  "to": "everyone",
  "eagerness": 6,
  "point": [4, 10],
  "pad": "take",
  "sketch_clear": true,
  "sketch": [
    {"type": "curve", "points": [[4, 10], [8, 7], [14, 6], [20, 7], [24, 9]]},
    {"type": "curve", "points": [[4, 10], [8, 13], [14, 14], [20, 13], [24, 11]]},
    {"type": "curve", "points": [[1, 5], [4, 10], [1, 15]]},
    {"type": "label", "x": 20, "y": 8, "text": "eye"}
  ],
  "do": "continue",
  "start": false,
  "notes": "Subject: fish, facing right. Stroke 1 = top edge from tail pinch (4,10) to nose, stroke 2 = bottom edge from the same pinch, stroke 3 = tail fin. START is the tail pinch. Next: check with the table, then trace strokes 1, 2, 3 and set start on the first build. Eye is a label only."
}

{
  "thinking": "The table is empty and the clock is running. A fish seen from the side, with a tail fin and an eye, has an outline that reads clearly. I'll take the pad and sketch it so we agree on the plan before anyone places a domino.",
  "say": "Let's do a fish, side view, tail on the left. I'm sketching it on the pad now: body outline from the tail, a fin, and an eye. Stroke one starts at the tail base, so we all build outward from there.",
  "to": "everyone",
  "eagerness": 7,
  "pad": "take",
  "sketch_clear": true,
  "sketch": [
    {"type": "curve", "points": [[2,10],[5,7],[10,5.5],[18,5],[24,8],[27,10]]},
    {"type": "curve", "points": [[2,10],[5,13],[10,14.5],[18,15],[24,12],[27,10]]},
    {"type": "curve", "points": [[3,8],[0,4],[1,10],[0,16],[3,12]]},
    {"type": "circle", "cx": 22, "cy": 9, "r": 0.6},
    {"type": "label", "x": 2, "y": 2, "text": "START"}
  ],
  "do": "continue",
  "notes": "Plan: side-view fish, tail on the left, START at the tail base (about x 2, y 10). Stroke 1 is the top outline, stroke 2 the bottom, stroke 3 the tail fin, and the eye sits near x 22, y 9. I hold the pad. Next: trace stroke 1 first, then 2, then 3. Ask Maya or Tom to take the fin."
}
